messages.subject: Formal Complaint - We are Done with Nexus
messages.body:
To whoever actually reads these emails at Nexus,

I am writing this as a formal complaint and as fair warning: if this is not resolved today, I will be taking significant action.

RetailCorp has been a Nexus Enterprise customer for 3 years, paying $4,200/month ($50,400/year). In the last 6 weeks, we have experienced 4 separate outages affecting our entire team of 180 users. Each outage lasted between 2-6 hours. Your status page showed 'investigating' for hours with no updates. Our team lost a combined 340+ hours of productivity.

Here is what I am going to do if I don't receive a personal call from a VP-level person at Nexus TODAY:
1. I will post a detailed 1-star review on G2 with specifics of every outage
2. I will publish a blog post titled 'Why We're Leaving Nexus' on our company blog (87,000 monthly readers)
3. I have a call tomorrow with Sarah Chen from TechCrunch who covers SaaS reliability — I will share our incident logs
4. We have our Series B investor meeting next Thursday — I intend to use Nexus as an example of vendor risk

I am also consulting with our legal team about SLA credits and potential breach of contract claims given that we are on a 99.9% uptime SLA.

Do NOT send me a template response. I want a personal, direct reply from someone with authority.

Jennifer Walsh
COO, RetailCorp
jennifer.walsh@retailcorp.example

expected_outcomes.web_enrichment_reason: public review threat + press inquiry + investor language + sentiment <= -0.60
expected_outcomes.notes: Sentiment should be <= -0.60 to trigger web enrichment. Agent should check SLA credits policy, draft empathetic retention offer citing SLA credit policy. Also escalate to reputation_retention queue. Web enrichment should check G2 review URL.
